snapshot.text: Aena, the Spanish airport operator, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} in FY2024, with Fitch raising its long-term rating and Moody's moving its outlook to positive.
Net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{net_leverage@FY2024}} as EBITDA rose by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}.

The point to watch is cash liquidity, which fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} of revenue, below the peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2024}}.

credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}} on revenue up {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}}, and operating profit rose by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}}.

Total debt was reduced by {{total_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{total_debt@FY2024}} and net debt by {{net_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{net_debt@FY2024}}, taking gross leverage down by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2024}}.

Cash generation strengthened: FFO rose by {{ffo.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo@FY2024}}, lifting FFO to debt by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}}, and free cash flow increased by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}}.
FCF to debt rose by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}}, helped by capex intensity easing by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}.
Interest coverage eased by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, still well above the peer median of {{interest_coverage.peer_median@FY2024}}.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2024}} to {{passengers@FY2024}}, with traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} below the {{traffic_growth@FY2023}} of FY2023.

Aeronautical revenue per passenger increased by {{aero_revenue_per_passenger.change@FY2024}} to {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}}, with the CNMC setting the maximum adjusted annual revenue per passenger for 2025 unchanged versus the prior year.
The EBITDA margin widened by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}, as revenue growth outpaced the rise in operating costs.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, taking cash liquidity to revenue down by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}.
In FY2023 the group held liquidity of {{liquidity@FY2023}}, including {{undrawn_facilities@FY2023}} of undrawn committed credit facilities, equal to {{liquidity_to_revenue@FY2023}} of revenue.
Funding conditions improved with the rating actions: Fitch upgraded the long-term and EMTN programme rating and Moody's moved the outlook to positive.

peer_positioning.text: Aena has the highest EBITDA margin of the airport peers ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2024}}), at {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}} against a median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@FY2024}}, and the strongest interest coverage ({{interest_coverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}).
Cash generation also leads the group, with FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}} and FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}} both ranking {{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2024}}.

Leverage sits in the middle of the group, with net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2024}} and gross leverage of {{gross_leverage@FY2024}}, while cash liquidity to revenue is the weakest of the peers ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2024}}).

watch_items.text: Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}, below the peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2024}} and the weakest of the group.
Cash: cash and cash-like investments declined by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}} as debt was repaid, so the buffer against maturities is thinner than a year earlier.
Coverage: interest coverage eased by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, a move to monitor even though it remains above the peer median.

Traffic: growth slowed by {{traffic_growth.change@FY2024}} to {{traffic_growth@FY2024}}, and the CNMC left the maximum adjusted annual revenue per passenger for 2025 unchanged, limiting tariff-led revenue growth.
